title: General pathology
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Explain cell injury, adaptation and death, acute and chronic inflammation and repair, edema, thrombosis, embolism and shock, genetic, pediatric and immune pathology, amyloidosis, neoplasia, environmental and nutritional disease, and laboratory medicine.

weeks.10: Neoplasia: grading, staging and tumor markers

blocks.deliverable: Match five types of necrosis to their causes and settings.
Explain the cardinal signs at the vascular and cellular level.
Apply Virchow's triad and compare the types of shock.
Week 7 midterm; explain the types of amyloid and their organs.
Compare grading and staging and the proper uses of tumor markers.
Interpret a basic metabolic panel and a complete blood count.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Pathology case conference: for three supplied cases, link the gross and microscopic findings to the mechanism and the clinical course.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
